drhp.business: Arisinfra Solutions Limited operates a B2B digital platform that aggregates demand, connects it to a distributed vendor network, and manages procurement, delivery, documentation, and credit in real time. The company serves developers, contractors, and suppliers across India, transforming manual, transaction-driven construction procurement into a coordinated, data-driven system. ARIS also provides contract manufacturing supply assurance and a Developer-as-a-Service (DaaS) execution model for landowners and real estate developers.
drhp.end_markets: Infrastructure (roads, railways, urban infrastructure, logistics, industrial corridors)|Real estate (residential, premium and luxury housing)|India (23 states and UTs, 1,100+ pincodes)
drhp.expansion: Arisinfra operates an asset-light model and does not own manufacturing assets. Its capacity expansion is driven by securing long-term reserved capacity through partner plants under its Contract Manufacturing segment. As of FY 2025-26, total reserved capacity reached 9 Million+ MTPA, comprising 6.1 million MT in Aggregates, 2.7 million MT in Ready-Mix Concrete, and 0.3 million MT in Asphalt. The company plans to deepen this network of plant relationships across these categories to strengthen supply assurance and margin expansion. risks.note: High likelihood and high impact; customers may delay or default on payments, with receivable cycles often longer than payable cycles, creating cash flow strain.
54% of revenue from Maharashtra and 29% from Tamil Nadu creates susceptibility to regional regulatory, political, or climate disruptions.
A few large vendors contribute a significant share of supplies, and vendors may fail to supply consistently, causing quality or delivery issues that affect fulfilment.
Misalignment between receivable and payable cycles creates cash flow challenges, exacerbated by high-growth operations.
Well-funded new entrants may erode market share or compress margins, threatening the company's position in the construction materials procurement space.
Stakeholders may be slow to adopt digital procurement tools, potentially limiting the scalability and efficiency gains of the platform.
Changes in GST, environmental, or mining regulations could affect sourcing, pricing, or operational viability.
